lines.text: What was daily life like in American cities just one hundred and fifty years ago before indoor plumbing?
It was vastly dirtier and more perilous than anyone realizes.
Every family kept porcelain chamber pots beneath their beds for nighttime calls of nature.
In the morning, people dumped the contents into wooden backyard outhouses or straight into city street gutters.
Raw waste seeped into shallow well drinking water, sparking deadly cholera and typhoid fever epidemics.
Baths were a luxury taken once a week, sharing the same heated kettle water among multiple family members.
Indoor plumbing and sanitary sewer networks saved more human lives than almost any medical invention in history.
